summary: The Spark sync notes list highlights including removal of Spark 3.4 support, the upgrade to Spark 4.1.2, a rest.catalog-purge property for DROP TABLE PURGE and deprecating SparkFilters in favor of SparkV2Filters. Discussion covered the Spark versioning strategy with accelerated Spark releases, with a suggested policy of one LTS plus two minors and a question of whether to support 3.5, 4.1 and 4.2 and remove 4.0, keeping CI burden in mind. CI usage improvements were summarized: parallel Spark test execution cut the run from about 84 to 58 minutes, plus a single Gradle cache writer, reduced test data volume and incremental PR matrix selection. Review requests carried over from the previous sync.

topics.title: Highlights
topics.summary: Spark 3.4 support was removed and Spark 4.1 was upgraded to 4.1.2. Other merges bind parameters in IcebergSparkSqlExtensionsParser, add ignore_missing_files to the migrate procedure, add a rest.catalog-purge property to delegate DROP TABLE PURGE, deprecate SparkFilters in favor of SparkV2Filters, and fix first row ID carry-over for manifest rewrite.

topics.title: Spark versioning going forward
topics.summary: The discussion followed the dev list thread on Spark versioning strategy with accelerated Spark releases. The points listed are a policy of one LTS plus two minors (at most three Spark versions), whether that means 3.5, 4.1 and 4.2 with 4.0 removed, and what to follow going forward while keeping the CI burden in mind. The notes pose these as questions and record no decision.
open_questions: Should Iceberg support one LTS plus two minor Spark versions (3.5, 4.1 and 4.2), removing 4.0?
What Spark version policy should be followed going forward?

topics.title: CI usage
topics.summary: Parallel Spark test execution merged on May 18, splitting the Spark matrix into concurrent core and extensions jobs and cutting the run from about 84 to 58 minutes. A single Gradle cache writer stops about ten jobs racing to write overlapping caches against the 10 GB cap. In flight are a PR reducing TestRewriteDataFilesAction data volume and one selecting PR matrices incrementally from changed files, with Java 17 as the primary PR JVM and full coverage on main, release and tags. The group also asked whether some tests could use in-memory FileIO, perhaps by switching the default FileIO to see if anything breaks.
open_questions: Can in-memory FileIO be used for some tests, for example by switching the default FileIO to see what breaks?

topics.title: Review requests
topics.summary: A new request is the PR parallelizing the RewriteManifests added-manifest copy path. Carried over from last time are the RewriteTablePath fixes, CALL older_than with function expressions, and the three sort PRs; the SupportsReportOrdering and K-way merge rewrite strategy PRs are noted as being reviewed.
